Remember djälthirri (to want) and marŋgithirri (to know) from Lesson 15? I told you they behave a bit differently. Well, here's their secret: they're not lone wolves. They're part of one of the most productive patterns in the whole language.

The suffix -thirri (or -dhirri after a nasal sound) takes an adjective, or a noun, or almost any state, and turns it into a verb of becoming.

djäl (in want of) → djälthirri → to come to want
marŋgi (knowing) → marŋgithirri → to come to know, to learn

And now watch it open up:

djulŋi (happy) → djulŋithirri → to become happy
Walala djulŋithina → They became happy

gorrmur' (hot) → gorrmur'thirri → to become hot
Gapu gorrmur'thina → The water got hot

borum (ripe) → borumdhirri → to become ripe (nasal ending, so -dhirri)
rakuny (dead) → rakunydhirri → to die, to become dead
galki (near) → galkithirri → to approach, to become close

And here's one that made me smile when I first saw it:
rerri (sickness) → rerrimirri (having sickness, Lesson 4!) → rerrimirrithirri → to become sick
Ŋayi rerrimirrithina → He got sick

Look at that word. Three layers deep: sickness → with-sickness → becoming-with-sickness. The suffixes stack like sediment, each one adding a stratum of meaning. This is the compound-image logic from Lesson 16 again, but now it's verbs all the way down.

These become-verbs live in Group 6, and their past form ends in -thina / -dhina, which you'll now start recognising everywhere:
djulŋithina, gorrmur'thina, rerrimirrithina, galkithirrina.

English does a faint version of this with -en: darken, soften, harden, ripen. Hebrew does it with whole verb patterns (nif'al, hitpa'el), Turkish with -laş (güzelleşmek, to become beautiful). But few languages do it as cleanly as Gupapuyŋu: take the state, add the becoming, done.

And think about what that means for the worldview. Nothing here is frozen. Any quality, hot, near, ripe, knowing, wanting, is one suffix away from being a process. The language assumes transformation. States are just slow verbs.

You are not sick. You became sick, and you can become well.
You are not ignorant. You are one -thirri away from knowing.
